## Prepare data for uncertainty analysis

```{r EF caluclation}

load("../Input/US_Direct_2018-2022.RData") #SiteData

USData <- USData %>%
  mutate(coef1 = 0.003252,
         coef2 = 6.74188,
         NSEF  = 1.55)
  
load



```



```{r }
#Calculate the EF
apply_factors_and_run <- function(f_row, base_df) {
  adj_df <- base_df %>%
    mutate(
      Fert_LCA_kg = Fert_LCA_kg * f_row$Fert_LCA_kg,
      P           = P           * f_row$P,
      PE          = PE          * f_row$PE,
      Topo        = Topo        * f_row$Topo,
      Frac_Fine   = Frac_Fine   * f_row$Frac_Fine,
      Frac_Medium = Frac_Medium * f_row$Frac_Medium,
      Frac_Coarse = Frac_Coarse * f_row$Frac_Coarse,
      coef1       = coef1       * f_row$coef1,
      coef2       = coef2       * f_row$coef2,
      NSEF        = NSEF        * f_row$NSEF
    ) %>%                                # ---- renormalise fractions ----
    mutate(total = Frac_Fine + Frac_Medium + Frac_Coarse,
           across(starts_with("Frac_"), ~ .x / total),
           .keep = "unused")

  # Your emission-factor calculation
  out <- N2OEF_direct(adj_df)

  # Return something tidy: add sim_id so we can identify the run
  tibble(sim_id = f_row$sim_id, result = out)
}

plan(multisession)          # use all available cores (Windows-safe)

results_df <- future_map_dfr(
  1:nrow(lhs_df),           # iterate over the 1 000 simulations
  ~ apply_factors_and_run(lhs_df[.x, ], USData),
  .progress = TRUE          # nice progress bar in RStudio
)
```
